notes: Read help page (Vlagtwedde-Vlaardingen FEV1, van der Lende et al. 1981). Long form, 133 men, 1-7 FEV1 measures each; id = subject. FLW (Applied Longitudinal Analysis, 2nd ed.) ch 8 linear mixed model of FEV1 decline with time by smoking status; design documented, exact model not at hand so medium.

formula: logfev1 ~ ht + age + baseht + baseage + (1 | id)
notes: Read help page (Six Cities Study, Topeka girls; Dockery et al. 1983). Long form, 300 girls, 1-12 visits; id = girl. logfev1 is log(FEV1), the raw FEV1 not in the table. FLW lung-growth linear mixed model of log FEV1 on height and age; baseht/baseage are time-invariant baseline values. medium.

Read help page (two-period three-treatment crossover for tension headache; Laird, Skinner & Kenward 1992). y = average pain relief; trt is a string factor (A/B/P). id = subject (2 periods each), center a multi-centre cluster kept per the #24 repeating-cluster rule though the crossover model uses subject only; 'sequence' left to columns.csv. Model inferred, low.

Read help page (DMPA contracepting-women trial, amenorrhea over four 90-day intervals; Machin et al. 1988). Long form, 1151 women, y binary (missing after dropout). FLW ch 14 (GLMM) logistic random-intercept example: logit P(amenorrhea) = b_i + trt + time + time^2; the quadratic time term is not a column so time is named once. high.

Read help page (CDC Georgia linked births; Neuhaus & Kalbfleisch 1998, Rabe-Hesketh & Skrondal 2008). 878 mothers x 5 births; mid = mother, cid = child/row id (ignored). Maternal age is the within-subject covariate of interest, birth order the occasion. Between/within-cluster model documented, exact spec not at hand, medium.

formula: logcd4 ~ group + week + group:week + age + sex + (week | id)
notes: Read help page (ACTG 193A AIDS trial; Henry et al. 1998). 1309 patients, 1-9 CD4 measures; id = patient, logcd4 = log(CD4+1) (raw not in table). group = 4 treatment arms (declared categorical). FLW ch 8 piecewise/linear random-slope model of log CD4 on week by treatment; medium.

Read help page (toenail onychomycosis trial; De Backer et al. 1998, Lesaffre & Spiessens 2001). 294 patients, binary onycholysis. FLW ch 14 (GLMM) logistic random-intercept: y ~ trt + month + trt:month + (1|id); visit is the redundant visit index (ignored). high. Likely folds with the Stata/geepack/faraway toenail exports.

Read help page (PdG hormone profiles over the menstrual cycle; Brumback & Rice 1998). 51 cycles from 51 women (22 conceptive, 29 non-conceptive); id = woman/cycle, logp = log PdG (raw not in table), group = conceptive vs not. Published model is a smoothing-spline curve model not expressible in lme4; filed as a random-slope approximation at low.

Read help page (NIMH Schizophrenia Collaborative Study; Gibbons & Hedeker 1994, Hedeker & Gibbons 2006). y = 4-level ordinal severity, weeks 0/1/3/6; id = patient. Random-effects ordinal/probit model documented; Hedeker uses sqrt(week) as the time axis (a transform of week). medium.

formula: y ~ trt + year + age + skin + gender + exposure + (1 | center) + (1 | center:id)
notes: Read help page (Skin Cancer Prevention Study, beta-carotene; Greenberg et al. 1990). 1683 subjects, y = count of new skin cancers per year (Poisson). id = subject, center kept as a higher cluster per the #24 repeating-cluster rule though FLW ch 14 uses subject only. medium.

Read help page (body-fat accretion around menarche; Phillips et al. 2003). pbf = percent body fat, time = years since menarche (positive or negative); id = girl, ~6.4 measures each. FLW piecewise-linear (knot at menarche) random-slope model; piecewise term not expressible so time named once. age/agemen (the raw components of time) stay in columns.csv. medium.

Read help page (Muscatine Coronary Risk Factor Study obesity; Woolson & Clarke 1984). y = obese 0/1 (missing allowed), biennial occasions; id = child. GLMM/GEE logistic on gender and an age polynomial by gender; age^2 not a column so age named once. occasion and baseage are alternate time axes left in columns.csv. medium.

Read help page (two-period crossover, cerebrovascular deficiency, ECG abnormality side-effect; Jones & Kenward 1989). y binary, 67 patients x 2 periods; id = subject, seq = treatment sequence (left in columns.csv). Random-intercept logistic rendering of the crossover; model inferred, low.

Read help page (UK malignant-melanoma mortality vs UVB; Langford, Bentham & McDonald 1998). 70 counties nested in 11 regions; observed = death count, expected = offset, county = one row each (ignored, cannot be a grouping factor). FLW multilevel Poisson with region random intercept. medium.

formula: postscore ~ prescore + curriculum + tvprevent + curriculum:tvprevent + (1 | sid) + (1 | sid:cid)
notes: Read help page (Television School and Family Smoking Prevention project; Flay et al. 1995). 1600 students in classes (cid) in schools (sid), 2x2 design CC x TV. postscore = tobacco-health-knowledge scale (0-4); filed continuous (FLW ch 22 three-level linear model), also modelled ordinal by Hedeker. prescore is the baseline covariate. medium.

Read help page (NTP ethylene-glycol developmental-toxicity study; Price et al. 1985). id = litter, multiple fetuses per litter. malform = fetal malformation (binary), the teratology outcome, with the litter random intercept (dose-response). Second outcome weight filed as model 2; weight ignored here. medium.

Second response of the NTP litter data: fetal weight (continuous) over the same litter grouping, a distinct response from the malformation model (model 1), so a separate model_index row; malformation ignored here. medium.

Read help page (insomnia clinical trial; Francom, Chuang-Stein & Landis 1989, Agresti 2002 Table 11.4). y = 4-level ordinal time-to-fall-asleep at baseline and 2 weeks; id = patient. Repeated cumulative-logit model with treatment-by-time interaction as the key test. medium.
